raw: {"diagnosis": "LVH", "stemi": "no", "rationale": "The precordial leads have very high voltage, with deep S waves in V2–V3 (about 25 mm or more) and tall R waves in V4–V6, plus a strain pattern of downsloping ST depression and T inversion in V5–V6; the ST elevation in V1–V3 sits opposite the deep S waves, so it is secondary to LVH and not a STEMI (the rhythm also looks irregular, which raises possible atrial fibrillation)."}

parsed.rationale: The precordial leads have very high voltage, with deep S waves in V2–V3 (about 25 mm or more) and tall R waves in V4–V6, plus a strain pattern of downsloping ST depression and T inversion in V5–V6; the ST elevation in V1–V3 sits opposite the deep S waves, so it is secondary to LVH and not a STEMI (the rhythm also looks irregular, which raises possible atrial fibrillation).
